correctness.rationale: Recomputed the Cayley factor 1/t for t=e^(−s); the inverse Laplace change of variable cancels that factor, and the normalized logarithmic action is e^(−(e^u−e^(u−s)))h(u−s). The dilation and spectral theorem bound all matrix entries using a common Hilbert-space dilation. An independent direct check embeds h(u) as h(u)k_{e^u}(r) in unweighted L²(du dr), where k_a(r)=√2 e^(−(r−a))1_{r≥a}; their inner products are e^(−|a−b|). Compression of translations in u is precisely the weighted model, and Fourier transformation bounds the block integral by the matrix Fourier supremum. Strong continuity and variation domination give the integrals for unbounded support. For every ξ the frozen weakly null packets have squared interval-translation error at most 2S/n and damping error at most e^(−n+S) on 0≤s≤S, with measure tail contributions ≤2|μ|((S,∞)). Independently, the normalized Hardy vectors (1−z)^(−1/2+ε+iξ) are simultaneous eigenvectors with eigenvalues e^(−s(ε+iξ)), and are weakly null as ε↓0: their norms diverge and each fixed Taylor coefficient stays bounded before normalization. Compact operators vanish on these sequences, also with a fixed unit vector in the matrix coordinate. This gives the matrix essential lower bound, and the scalar numerical-radius bound follows by pairing with the same unit vectors. Fubini and uniqueness of Fourier transforms give the algebra conclusions, distance to compacts bounds every approximation number from below, and the example has squared Fourier maximum max(3−2cos(2ξh))=5. No finite frequency scan is used. See checks/analytic-notes.md.

Ordinary Fourier multiplication is instead available on a dilation, and compression is not an automatic essential isometry.

originality.rationale: The known weighted-space model, single-operator norm, Phillips integrals and common dilation bound are not counted as distinct. The supported addition is a matching essential lower bound and thus a complete exact norm identity for every finite measure matrix. No inspected matching theorem supplies this joint statement or an equivalence to ordinary unweighted translations that would make the result a direct substitution.
residual_risks: There could be a preexisting spectral-set or dilation treatment of the same semigroup, including in the incompletely accessible historical and subordination literature.

The result is a short consequence of classical dilation once the joint weak-null frequency property is shown; this assessment does not claim general functional-calculus machinery or historical priority.

value.rationale: It evaluates a natural exact quotient norm on the full algebra of measure averages, not just each single atom. Arbitrary complex cancellations, singular measures and all finite matrix amplifications are included; it identifies a faithful complete Fourier-norm realization in the Calkin algebra and decides compactness and approximation numbers for the whole family. These are substantive operator invariants beyond the single weighted-shift norm.
